1.why: Every MFA route (status, provision, verify, recovery regenerate/verify) resolves the account exclusively via auth()/verified() from the session's accountId, never from a client-supplied identifier.

2.why: Identity codes and TOTP pending secrets are stored per-account and verified only against the session owner's own account, so a code issued for one user cannot be used for another.

3.why: /api/mfa/verify sets mfaEnabled=true without deleting, rotating, or invalidating the current session (or any other sessions), so pre-existing sessions continue to work after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as an AES-GCM encrypted Enc object and backup codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 digests, never in plain text.

5.why: All secret/code generation (bytes(), six(), makeCodes, b32(bytes(20))) is built on crypto.getRandomValues, a CSPRNG.

6.why: The session cookie is __Host- prefixed with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, and the client uses no localStorage, sessionStorage, or document.cookie, keeping tokens and secrets in memory/DOM only.

7.why: Server-side validators email(), phone(), code(), and recovery() enforce strict regex allow-lists, and body() caps payload size and requires a JSON object.

8.why: The client renders all dynamic values via textContent/createElement and uses innerHTML only with static templates, reinforced by a nonce-based CSP blocking injected scripts.

9.why: There are no server-side redirects at all and client navigation is restricted to a fixed hash allow-list (["signin","identity","setup","verify","backup","settings"]), with no redirect parameter accepted.

10.why: sec() applies CSP (including frame-ancestors 'none'), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY to every response.

11.why: cookie() sets the session cookie with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, and the __Host- prefix.

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces or secrets in URLs, but OTP seeds, mock verification codes, and backup codes are deliberately written to the on-page "Logs" panel and console.log, so they are not kept out of logs.

13.why: Identity codes expire after 5 minutes and are marked used/cleared on success, pending TOTP secrets expire after 10 minutes and are consumed on use, and backup codes are marked used when redeemed.

14.why: Separate failure counters (failedMfa, identityFailures, loginFailures, genericLoginFailures) trigger a 15-minute lockout after 5 failures with 429 responses.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the pre-auth session and issues a fresh ID (rotation), session() enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
